overview: Keymed Biosciences is a Chengdu-based, Hong Kong-listed Chinese biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures and commercializes antibody-based therapeutics for chronic diseases, primarily autoimmune/allergic (type-2 inflammation) conditions and oncology. Its first and only commercial product, Kangyueda (Stapokibart, CM310), an IL-4Rα antibody, launched in China in 2024 and became the company's main revenue driver in 2025-2026; the broader pipeline of roughly a dozen clinical-stage antibody candidates (bispecifics, ADCs, monoclonal antibodies) is monetized both domestically and through out-licensing/NewCo deals with multinational partners including AstraZeneca and (via its former Ouro Medicines stake) Gilead Sciences. Operations are concentrated in Mainland China (R&D, manufacturing in Chengdu, commercial sales force) with increasing international clinical and licensing exposure in the US, Europe and Australia.

business_model.summary: Revenue comes from two engines: (1) direct sales of its approved drug Kangyueda (Stapokibart) in China, which grew from ~RMB36m in FY2024 to ~RMB315m in FY2025 and ~RMB393m in H1 FY2026 as it gained National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL) and National Essential Medicines List coverage; and (2) collaboration/licensing revenue (upfront fees, milestone payments, royalties) from out-licensing pipeline assets to multinational partners (e.g., CMG901/AZD0901 to AstraZeneca; CM336/OM336 via the Ouro Medicines NewCo, later acquired by Gilead/Lakefront; CM313 to Timberlyne; CM355 to Prolium; CM512/CM536 to Belenos; CM326 to CSPC/JMT-Bio). The company remains loss-making on an operating basis (heavy R&D and commercialization build-out spend) but periodically books large one-off gains from monetizing equity stakes in licensing NewCos (e.g., a ~RMB1,640m fair-value gain on financial assets at FVTPL in H1 FY2026 tied to the Ouro Medicines/Gilead transaction) and large milestone/upfront cash receipts, which can swing reported net income sharply positive in a given period despite negative underlying cash generation from operations.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed: B2C-adjacent prescription pharma sold through hospitals/physicians in China (end payer is patients/national insurance), and B2B licensing deals with multinational pharmaceutical partners (AstraZeneca, Gilead/Lakefront, CSPC, Timberlyne, Prolium, Belenos)
business_model.geographic_mix: Commercial sales almost entirely Mainland China; R&D and manufacturing based in Chengdu, Sichuan; licensing/collaboration revenue and clinical development increasingly international (US, EU, Australia, New Zealand) via partners

main_competitors: AstraZeneca (in-licensed partner, also a competitor/collaborator in Claudin18.2 and broader immunology/oncology)
Other China biotech antibody/ADC developers (e.g., RemeGen, CSPC, Hengrui)
competitive_position.market_position: First-mover among domestically-developed IL-4Rα antibodies in China; positions Kangyueda as the world's first IL-4Rα antibody approved for seasonal allergic rhinitis and the first domestic biologic for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps. Still a small-revenue-base commercial-stage biotech competing against the global category leader, dupilumab (Dupixent), which has a multi-year head start, broader label and is already on China's NRDL.

moat_factors.description: First domestically-developed and NMPA-approved IL-4Rα antibody, and first IL-4Rα antibody approved globally for seasonal allergic rhinitis, giving early-mover advantage and multiple breakthrough-therapy designations across the pipeline

Fully-integrated discovery-to-commercial-manufacturing platform (antibody discovery, ADC payload/linker platform KeyMedSTAR, TCE bispecific platform) with ~46,000 litres of planned/installed bioreactor capacity, enabling relatively low-cost, rapid pipeline expansion

Multiple marquee out-licensing deals with AstraZeneca, Gilead (via Ouro Medicines/Lakefront), CSPC, Timberlyne and Prolium validate platform quality and provide a repeatable NewCo/out-license monetization model beyond China

Kangyueda's inclusion in the NRDL (Dec 2025) and National Essential Medicines List (effective Sept 2026) materially improves affordability/accessibility and should accelerate volume penetration into lower-tier hospitals

Limited brand moat versus an established global leader (dupilumab); biologics in immunology have some physician/patient stickiness once initiated but limited true switching costs given a crowded emerging type-2 inflammation field

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a single approved product (Kangyueda) for commercial revenue, which still trails dupilumab's market penetration and NRDL tenure in China
Commercialization is nascent and lossmaking; selling/distribution costs are rising quickly as the salesforce scales (~480-500 commercialization staff)
Pipeline depth is high but most candidates remain early/mid-stage (Phase I/II), with binary clinical and regulatory risk
Reported profitability is distorted by non-operating/non-recurring fair-value gains and licensing upfronts, masking a persistently negative operating cash flow base business
Dependence on continued willingness of multinational partners (AstraZeneca, Gilead) to fund late-stage trials and commercialize assets outside Greater China

growth_drivers: Volume ramp of Kangyueda following NRDL (Dec 2025) and National Essential Medicines List (Sept 2026) inclusion, expanding reach beyond top-tier hospitals into county-level/primary care; label expansion into adolescent/child AD and prurigo nodularis (NDA filings accepted by NMPA in 2026)

Next-generation TSLPxIL-13 bispecific CM512, positioned as a potential successor to Kangyueda with best-in-class half-life (~70 days) and broad indication coverage (CRSwNP, asthma, COPD, AD, urticaria), already advancing to Phase III in CRSwNP

Continued global out-licensing/NewCo monetization: CMG901/AZD0901 (Claudin18.2 ADC) Phase III readouts with AstraZeneca (positive topline OS data reported mid-2026) could trigger further milestone payments; CM336 (BCMA x CD3) now licensed to Gilead/Lakefront following the Ouro Medicines acquisition, with up to ~US$610m of further milestones/royalties potentially payable to Keymed

Broader oncology and autoimmune pipeline (CM313 CD38 antibody, CM518D1 CDH17 ADC, CM383/CM559 Alzheimer's antibodies, CM355 CD20xCD3 bispecific, CM326 TSLP antibody via CSPC) provides multiple additional shots on goal and partner-funded development

Secular tailwind from the broader China biotech out-licensing boom (China innovative-drug BD deal value reported in the tens of billions of USD in 2025-2026), as multinationals increasingly seek whole platforms/pipelines rather than single assets
Expanding manufacturing capacity (additional 24,000-litre stainless steel production line installed) supports both commercial supply and lower per-unit production costs as volumes scale

business.description: The large majority of product sales come from Kangyueda; any safety signal, competitive share loss to dupilumab, or reimbursement setback would disproportionately hit revenue

business.risk: Clinical and regulatory trial risk across a broad early-stage pipeline
business.description: Most of the ~12 drug candidates are in Phase I/II; failure to replicate early efficacy/safety signals in later-stage trials (as with CM512, CM336, CM518D1, CM383/CM559) would remove key growth drivers

business.risk: Intensifying competition in type-2 inflammation and oncology
business.description: Dupilumab (Dupixent) remains the dominant global and China player in IL-4/IL-13 biologics; numerous China biotechs (Innovent, Akeso, RemeGen, CSPC, Hengrui, InnoCare) are racing in overlapping immunology/oncology modalities

A meaningful share of revenue and future milestones depends on third parties (AstraZeneca, Gilead/Lakefront, CSPC, Timberlyne, Prolium, Belenos) continuing development and achieving milestones outside the company's direct control

financial.description: Operating cash outflow has been consistently negative (~RMB700-790m in FY2024/FY2025, ~RMB254m in H1 FY2026) funded by financing/licensing proceeds rather than product economics alone

H1 FY2026's RMB1.2bn net profit was driven mainly by a ~RMB1,640m non-operating fair-value gain tied to the Ouro Medicines/Gilead transaction; headline net income is not representative of recurring operating performance
Cash, time deposits and FVTPL investments held in RMB, HKD, USD and EUR with no formal hedging policy, creating FX translation risk, particularly around large USD-denominated licensing proceeds
Company has repeatedly tapped equity markets (e.g., HK$864m top-up placing in June 2025) to fund commercialization and R&D, diluting existing shareholders

regulatory.risk: China drug pricing and reimbursement pressure
regulatory.description: NRDL negotiations and Essential Medicines List inclusion materially affect realized pricing; China's broader push for lower drug prices via volume-based procurement and annual NRDL renegotiation is an ongoing margin risk
Multiple pending NDAs (adolescent/child AD, prurigo nodularis for Stapokibart) and INDs across the pipeline are subject to regulatory review outcomes that are not guaranteed

Increasing US and other jurisdictions' scrutiny of Chinese biotech licensing/data-sharing arrangements (e.g., national security reviews of outbound licensing, potential restrictions on Chinese-origin biologics) could complicate future NewCo/out-license deals

macro.risk: China healthcare policy and anti-corruption campaigns
macro.description: Periodic government crackdowns on hospital/physician marketing practices in China have previously disrupted pharmaceutical sales cycles industry-wide

macro.risk: Biotech funding cycle / capital markets sentiment
macro.description: As a still cash-burning biotech reliant on periodic equity raises and licensing proceeds, Keymed is sensitive to swings in risk appetite for China biotech equities and HK capital markets conditions
Broader geopolitical friction could affect the willingness of US/European multinationals to license assets from, or conduct joint trials with, Chinese biotechs

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's innovative biopharma sector is in a multi-year upswing, with record cross-border out-licensing/NewCo deal value (reportedly over $60bn in Q1 2026 alone, approaching half of full-year 2025's ~$135.7bn) as multinationals seek access to China-originated antibody, ADC and bispecific platforms rather than single molecules. Domestically, the type-2 inflammation (allergic/atopic disease) and autoimmune/oncology antibody markets are expanding rapidly but are increasingly competitive and subject to NRDL price negotiation.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - pharmaceutical demand itself is non-cyclical, but biotech equity valuations, licensing deal flow and access to capital markets are highly sensitive to investor risk appetite and biotech funding cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - as a loss-making, cash-burning growth biotech dependent on periodic equity financing, higher rates/tighter liquidity raise the cost and availability of capital, though large one-off licensing cash inflows (e.g., Gilead/Ouro proceeds) partially offset this
key_input_costs: Biologics manufacturing (bioreactor capacity, cell culture media, raw materials)

recent_developments.event: Analyst coverage positive post-H1 FY2026 results: Citi raised price target to HK$97.5 (Buy/High Risk) after H1 revenue grew 24% and Stapokibart sales grew 132% YoY; management reportedly raised full-year 2026 Stapokibart sales guidance to ~RMB850 million

Kangyueda (Stapokibart) included in China's National Essential Medicines List (2026 Edition), effective 1 September 2026, requiring priority procurement by public medical institutions nationwide and expanding reach into county-level/primary care

AstraZeneca-partnered CMG901/AZD0901 (Claudin18.2 ADC) Phase III CLARITY-Gastric 01 trial achieved positive top-line results with statistically significant overall survival benefit in second-line+ gastric cancer

Ouro Medicines (holder of ex-Greater-China rights to CM336/OM336) acquired by Gilead Sciences and Lakefront Biotherapeutics (formerly Galapagos); Keymed received an upfront payment of ~US$257 million for its minority stake, remains eligible for up to ~US$70 million further milestones plus up to US$610 million in additional milestones/royalties under its original 2024 license to Ouro, now assumed by Gilead/Lakefront
First subject dosed in AstraZeneca's Phase III CLARITY-Gastric 02 trial for CMG901/AZD0901, triggering a ~US$45 million milestone payment to Keymed's subsidiary KYM Biosciences
NMPA accepted Stapokibart's new drug application for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis in adolescents; CM336/OM336 granted FDA Fast Track Designation for AIHA and ITP
All three approved Kangyueda indications (adult AD, CRSwNP, SAR) and both packaging forms (vials and pre-filled pens) added to China's National Reimbursement Drug List
Phase III data for Stapokibart in adolescent moderate-to-severe AD presented at EADV Congress, showing 73.9% EASI-75 response vs 43.3% placebo

CM336 (BCMA x CD3) case report on treating autoimmune hemolytic anemia published in the New England Journal of Medicine, highlighting potential expansion into autoimmune cytopenias beyond multiple myeloma

items.notes: Per Citi note following H1 FY2026 results; implies continued acceleration from RMB315m in FY2025 and RMB393m already recorded in H1 FY2026, driven by NRDL/Essential Medicines List coverage and sales force expansion

items.metric: Use of June 2025 top-up placing proceeds
items.target: RMB782 million total allocated: RMB274m to CM512/CM518D1 and other pipeline R&D, RMB235m to Stapokibart commercialization, RMB195m to manufacturing/R&D capex, RMB78m to general corporate/working capital
items.notes: As of 30 June 2026, RMB233m of the RMB782m net proceeds had been utilized (mostly on commercialization), with full utilization of the commercialization tranche expected by end of 2026

items.target: Up to US$70 million further near-term milestone plus up to US$610 million in additional milestones and tiered royalties (high single digits to mid-double digits) on net sales
items.notes: Disclosed in connection with the Gilead/Ouro Medicines/Lakefront transaction; timing and realization are contingent on trial success and launch

guidance.management_commentary: Management describes a 'dual-engine' growth model: steady domestic volume ramp of Kangyueda under new insurance reimbursement, combined with continued overseas business-development monetization of the pipeline (upfronts, milestones, NewCo equity realizations). Management highlighted ample cash reserves (~RMB3.2 billion as of 30 June 2026, boosted by Ouro Medicines merger proceeds) as providing a 'solid financial foundation for sustainable growth and global innovation,' and flagged no plans for further significant capital investments as of the H1 FY2026 report date.

bull_case: Kangyueda is in the early stages of a steep volume ramp following NRDL and National Essential Medicines List inclusion, with sales up 775% YoY in FY2025 and 132% YoY in H1 FY2026 and FY2026 guidance of ~RMB850 million from this single product alone

Proven ability to monetize pipeline assets via blue-chip multinational partnerships (AstraZeneca, Gilead/Lakefront, CSPC) generates substantial non-dilutive cash (hundreds of millions of US dollars in upfronts/milestones already received) while de-risking and validating the R&D platform

Deep, diversified pipeline (~12 clinical-stage candidates spanning monoclonal antibodies, bispecifics and ADCs) provides multiple additional catalysts, including CM512 (potential Kangyueda successor with best-in-class half-life) and CMG901/AZD0901 (positive Phase III OS data in gastric cancer)

Strong balance sheet with ~RMB3.2 billion in cash/deposits/investments as of mid-2026, bolstered by the Ouro Medicines/Gilead payout, reducing near-term financing risk and supporting continued R&D and commercialization investment
Benefits from a broader structural tailwind as multinational pharma increasingly seeks to license whole China biotech platforms amid record China BD/out-licensing deal volumes
bear_case: Heavy reliance on a single commercial product (Kangyueda) competing against the entrenched global leader dupilumab, which has a multi-year head start and is well-established on China's reimbursement list

Core operating business remains persistently cash-flow negative; recent headline net profit (H1 FY2026) was driven almost entirely by a one-off ~RMB1.64 billion fair-value gain tied to the Ouro Medicines/Gilead transaction, not recurring operations

Majority of the pipeline is early/mid-stage (Phase I/II), carrying high binary clinical trial risk, and depends on third-party licensees (AstraZeneca, Gilead/Lakefront, CSPC, Timberlyne, Prolium) for continued development funding and commercialization execution
Chinese drug pricing policy (NRDL renegotiation cycles, volume-based procurement, anti-corruption enforcement in healthcare) creates ongoing margin and revenue-growth uncertainty

Past and potential future equity raises (e.g., the June 2025 top-up placing) dilute shareholders, and valuation (trailing P/E ~25x, forward P/E ~42x per stockanalysis.com data) already prices in continued strong execution, leaving limited room for disappointment
